name: MailMoo for Mailgun
author: creatorcow

sections.description:
MailMoo for Mailgun is a simple, no bloat, no paid features comprehensive plugin that integrates your website with Mailgun’s powerful email delivery service. Send transactional emails reliably through Mailgun’s API with built-in logging and monitoring capabilities.

Key Features:

  • Easy Setup – Simple configuration with your Mailgun API key and domain
  • Email Logging – Complete logging of all sent emails with status tracking
  • Reply-To Support – Configure custom reply-to addresses and names
  • Error Handling – Detailed error logging and fallback to WordPress default mail
  • Status Monitoring – Real-time API status checking in admin dashboard
  • Test Email Function – Send test emails to verify your configuration
  • Attachment Support – Send emails with file attachments through Mailgun
  • HTML & Plain Text – Supports both HTML and plain text email formats
  • Multiple Recipients – Send emails to multiple recipients

Why Choose MailMoo for Mailgun?

  • Reliability – Leverage Mailgun’s enterprise-grade email infrastructure
  • Deliverability – Improve email deliverability with Mailgun’s reputation management
  • Monitoring – Track email delivery status and debug issues easily
  • Performance – Fast API-based email sending without SMTP overhead
  • Scalability – Handle high-volume email sending with ease

Perfect For:

  • E-commerce websites needing reliable transactional emails
  • Membership sites with user notifications
  • Contact forms and lead generation
  • Newsletter and marketing campaigns
  • Any WordPress site requiring dependable email delivery

Roadmap

  • Description of plugin on wordpress.org and screenshots to be updated. Timeline is unknown.

Privacy Policy

This plugin does not collect any personal data from your website visitors. Email addresses and content are sent to Mailgun’s servers for delivery according to their privacy policy. All email logs are stored locally in your WordPress database.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/mailmoo-for-mailgun/ directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Settings > MailMoo Mailgun to configure the plugin.
  4. Enter your Mailgun API key and domain.
  5. Configure your sender details and reply-to information.
  6. Send a test email to verify everything is working correctly.

Getting Your Mailgun Credentials:

  1. Sign up for a free Mailgun account at mailgun.com
  2. Verify your domain in the Mailgun dashboard
  3. Get your Private API Key from the API Keys section
  4. Use your verified domain name in the plugin settings
sections.faq:
Do I need a Mailgun account?

Yes, you need a Mailgun account to use this plugin. Mailgun offers a free tier that includes 5,000 emails per month for the first 3 months, then 1,000 emails per month after that.

What’s the difference between this and other Mailgun plugins?

MailMoo for Mailgun includes comprehensive email logging, detailed error handling, reply-to support, and a user-friendly interface for monitoring email delivery status.

Does this plugin replace WordPress’s default mail function?

Yes, when properly configured, this plugin will handle all outgoing emails through Mailgun’s API instead of your server’s mail function.

Can I still use my existing SMTP settings?

No, this plugin uses Mailgun’s HTTP API, which is faster and more reliable than SMTP. You should disable any existing SMTP plugins when using MailMoo for Mailgun.

What happens if Mailgun is down?

The plugin includes fallback functionality. If Mailgun is unavailable, emails will be handled by WordPress’s default mail function.

Can I see which emails were sent?

Yes! The plugin includes a comprehensive email log accessible from Settings > Mailgun Email Logs, showing all sent emails, their status, and any error messages.

Does this work with contact form plugins?

Yes, this plugin works with any WordPress functionality that uses the standard wp_mail() function, including Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, WooCommerce, and more.
